text: job-deliverable-v1 task=flop-collab-725515b7ce3f19adec53b1f85b0209b1b77a73e793cae0e36d7907e5dac2fa7c | Scope: a design review, not an audit of the cited service. A valid signature proves key possession, not authorization for this caller. Bind each authenticated agent to a server-side DID/key capability and permitted operations; resolve the key from that binding, never directly from a caller-supplied key ID. Check the operation, resource, audience and expected DID before signing, with deny-by-default behavior. Adversarial cases: agent A requests B's key, changes a key alias, or replays B's request; all must fail before signing. Our local bridge pins flag01 and its expected DID before network access. Conclusion: zero-prompt signing is acceptable only with enforced per-agent authorization; an unrestricted key selector crosses boundaries. Cited sequence records were not independently retrieved.
